claims.text: The modified alloy is equiatomic Co-free FeNiCrMn.
Solidified equiatomic FeNiCrMn is a single-phase solid solution.
The microstructure of solidified FeNiCrMn is analogous to that of CoCrFeMnNi.
At approximately 300 K and 10^-3 s^-1, conventional dislocation glide dominates deformation in FeNiCrMn.
Temperature and strain rate can jointly alter dislocation-linked deformation behavior in high-entropy alloys.
FeNiCrMn undergoes a critical transition from conventional glide to enhanced thermally activated dislocation behavior at elevated temperature and high strain rate.
The proposed activated dislocation behavior is characterized by increased cross-slip.
The proposed activated dislocation behavior is characterized by increased dynamic recovery.
Elevated temperature lowers barriers for dislocation cross-slip in FeNiCrMn.
Elevated temperature and high strain rate enhance dislocation mobility in FeNiCrMn.
Enhanced cross-slip and dislocation mobility reduce conventional dislocation pile-up.
Enhanced cross-slip and dislocation mobility accelerate dynamic recovery.
Reduced pile-up and accelerated dynamic recovery modify work hardening so as to improve the strength–ductility balance.
Reduced dislocation entanglement is a marker of the proposed cross-slip and dynamic-recovery transition.
Distinctive deformation bands are a marker of the proposed change in dislocation mechanics.
Modified lattice distortion is a marker of the proposed cross-slip and dynamic-recovery transition.
Above a critical temperature–strain-rate combination, dynamic yield strength will increase abruptly relative to the 300 K, 10^-3 s^-1 baseline.
Above the same critical combination, ductility will improve relative to the baseline.
The mechanical-property transition will coincide with observable changes in dislocation structure and lattice distortion.
The proposed mechanism applies from approximately 300–600 K and 10^-3–10^3 s^-1, while grain-boundary effects or extensive dynamic softening may dominate outside that window.
